LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.1: LISTENING FOR DETAIL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How should one listen for detail?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify main ideas in a listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. respond appropriately to questions based on the listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the importance of listening for details in life. • Listen to a recorded text on wild life and answer questions from the text, and discuss the main ideas, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. • Listen to a passage read by peers or the teacher and outline the main ideas from the text individually, Discuss with peers answers based on a given text. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views. How should one listen for detail?

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.1: Listening for Detail together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication is promoted as the learner listens keenly and actively and responds to questions.

• Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner interacts with digital devices when listening to a recorded text.

60

Values:
• Patriotism is promoted as the learner nurtures the love of their country by interacting with texts on Kenya’s rich wildlife

heritage.

• Responsibility is promoted as the learner is sensitised on the importance of wildlife.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Wildlife Conservation is enhanced as the learner interacts with information about wildlife.

Link to other subjects:

The leaner develops listening for detail and is able to relate it to their learning in Kiswahili.

1. identify main ideas in a listening text,
2. respond appropriately to questions based on the listening text,
